unexpectedFinding.title: git worktree remove deregisters but silently fails to delete files on Windows MAX_PATH (260 char) paths — for both this run's removals and pre-existing debris from an earlier, unrelated incident
details: Every `.claude/worktrees/**` worktree hit `error: failed to delete '<path>': Filename too long` when removed with plain `git worktree remove` (and, for the 3 dirty ones, `--force`). git still deregisters the worktree from `.git/worktrees/` and from `git worktree list` — the failure is purely at the OS file-unlink step, caused by the combined length of `.claude/worktrees/<name>/src/DungeonFortress.Game/.godot/...` deep import-cache paths exceeding Windows' 260-character limit. `rm -rf` (MSYS) does not hit the same limit and was used to finish deleting the orphaned directory content after confirming (`git rev-parse --git-dir` failing with 'not a git repository') that git had already deregistered each one.

While clearing these, 6 directories were found in `.claude/worktrees/` that had ALREADY been deregistered before this task started — they never appeared in the initial `git worktree list --porcelain` snapshot (67 entries) taken at the top of this task, yet sat on disk with a `.git` pointer file referencing a `.git/worktrees/<name>` admin directory that no longer exists (agent-a67492ea35395b5d6, agent-hud-readability, agent-issue101, agent-tempo-rules), or with no git linkage at all (coord-verify110, review-pr108-base — leftover review-harness scratch dirs, not full checkouts). This is the same failure mode as above, from an earlier, unrelated `git worktree remove` run that predates this task. They were cleared in the same pass: each was independently confirmed already deregistered (git refuses to treat them as a repo), so removing their leftover files carries the same safety guarantee as the 29 this task itself deregistered — git's own dirty-check already ran and passed at the time they were removed, whenever that was.

This failure mode is a durable risk for this repository specifically because Godot worktrees carry `.godot` import caches with deep generated paths; any future `git worktree remove` on a `.claude/worktrees/**` (or any deeply-nested) Godot worktree can leave the same kind of filesystem debris even though `git worktree list` correctly shows it gone. Not fixed by this PR — named here as a finding, not remediated with a wrapper script, because AGENTS.md/scripts/verify.ps1 are out of this task's file partition and the fix (e.g. an `rm -rf` fallback wrapped around `git worktree remove`) belongs with whoever owns the worktree-creation tooling.
